clue.text: Aspiring scout, some years ago — ferocious type confronting copper, British

blocks.note: a wolf is a byword for a fierce, predatory creature
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
standard abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A would-be scout from decades back comes face to face with a fierce character and a British policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal. Wolf Cub was the old name for the junior branch of the Scouts, now called Cub Scouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Before the renaming in 1966, a boy hoping to join the Scouts started in the junior section as one of these.

clue.text: Wife to lend a hand with puppy

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for wife
to assist someone

explanation.surface: A wife pitches in to help look after the family's new puppy.
explanation.definitionFit: A whelp is a young dog, the word also used for the young of wolves and other carnivores.

clue.text: Gem found in organ by old friend

blocks.note: the liver is an internal organ
standard abbreviation for old
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A precious stone is discovered inside a body part, next to an old companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' simply places the friend next to the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Liver opal is a reddish-brown variety of opal, so it is a kind of gemstone.

clue.text: Penny leaving Mediterranean island with American chap?

indicators.note: something that leaves departs, so that letter goes out of the island's name

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for penny
Cyprus is an island in the eastern Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Penny departs a Mediterranean island alongside an American man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name but is the coin. The question mark admits the definition is by example: Cyrus is a typically American first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyrus is a man's first name much more common in the United States, so it names an example of an American fellow.

clue.text: Horrific descent? Sport must involve bit of danger

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so the sport wraps around the extra letter
only a small piece, the opening letter, of the following word is taken

blocks.note: descent in the sense of lineage or ancestry, as in noble blood
curling is a sport played by sliding stones on ice
first letter of danger

explanation.surface: A dreadful fall happens because a sport carries a hint of danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'descent' suggests a plunge, matching 'Horrific', but it means ancestry. Curling is played on ice by sliding heavy granite stones towards a target.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bloodcurdling is so terrifying it seems to chill the blood, which is what horrific describes.

clue.text: Reportedly fed up with panel

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: bored means weary and fed up

explanation.surface: Someone tells of being sick and tired of a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: A board is a group of people who govern or advise, the same as a panel of experts or directors.

clue.text: Ship's officer makes racket catching duck, one in Aussie river

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so the racket goes around the duck

blocks.note: a racket is a kind of bat
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, shaped like O
Roman numeral one
the Swan River flows through Perth in Western Australia

explanation.surface: A ship's officer creates a din while catching a duck, one of the birds on an Australian river.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions: the duck goes in the racket (B-O-AT), then 'one' goes in the river (SW-I-AN); 'in' is the second container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatswain, or bosun, is the petty officer in charge of a ship's rigging, anchors and deck crew.

clue.text: An animal's taken over joint

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking something over turns it upside down, so the animal is read bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
the elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: A creature has been seized, and it has hold of a bone joint.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is': the animal is taken over.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the hinge connecting the foot to the leg, a joint of the body.

clue.text: Madden, getting one dreadfully enraged

indicators.note: doing something dreadfully means badly, so the letters come out in a mess

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: To madden someone is to make them furious.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface links the definition to its own fodder: maddening someone does get them enraged.
explanation.definitionFit: To madden in the sense of driving someone insane is to derange them, unsettling their mind.

clue.text: One may see one upriver always carrying line

indicators.note: something carrying a load holds it inside, so the first word encloses the second

blocks.note: ever means always, as in for ever
standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A riverside walker notes that one is liable to spot something heading upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole cryptic phrase: young eels migrate up rivers from the sea, so an angler may see one swimming upriver.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvers are young eels, which travel in great numbers from the ocean up into freshwater rivers.

clue.text: Loire surprisingly blocked by container ship

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is unexpected, so the river's letters turn up in an unexpected order
something blocked has an obstruction sitting inside it, so the second item goes into the first

blocks.note: the French river, taken as anagram fodder
a tank is a container for liquids

explanation.surface: The river Loire is unexpectedly obstructed by a container vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'container ship' reads as one phrase but splits: 'container' is wordplay, 'ship' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil tanker is a ship built to carry petroleum in bulk.

clue.text: NCO in car park cut colonel off

indicators.note: cutting a phrase trims its end, so the final letter is lost
something gone off has gone wrong, so all the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: car park with its last letter removed
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A junior soldier in a car park snubs his colonel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like snubbing, but it docks the K from car park.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance corporal is the lowest rank of non-commissioned officer in the British Army.

clue.text: Left us keeled over and adrift on the Red Sea

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a place, standing for a noun

indicators.note: a boat that has keeled over is capsized, so the word is turned back to front
something adrift has come loose and is out of position, so its letters are scrambled

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
us written backwards
the word and, rearranged

explanation.surface: Sailors complain they were left capsized and drifting on the Red Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' that seems to join the two disasters is not a link: it is the letters being jumbled. Port is the nautical word for the left side.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Sudan is Sudan's main seaport, located on the Red Sea coast.

clue.text: Authoritarian writer of novels, abridged

indicators.note: an abridged text has been shortened, so the writer's name loses its last letter

blocks.note: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy

explanation.surface: A strict novelist has had his work cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: A stern person is strict and severe, the manner of an authoritarian figure who demands obedience.

clue.text: Photograph mate in front of superb cinema

blocks.note: a picture is a photograph
a pal is a mate
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: A photo shows a friend standing outside a splendid cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture palace is an old-fashioned British term for a grand movie theatre.

clue.text: Truce, widespread over in Cuba, still?

indicators.note: something knocked over is upset and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: C is Cuba's international vehicle registration code
to still pain is to ease it
rife means widespread

explanation.surface: A truce that once covered much of Cuba is still holding, or is it?
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: 'in' places the Cuba letter and 'still' before the jumbled widespread word. 'Still' looks like an adverb but is a verb, to calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceasefire is an agreed halt to fighting, which is what a truce is.

clue.text: Novel plant

blocks.note: first meaning: a 1922 novel by D. H. Lawrence
second meaning: a name for several tall flowering plants such as mullein

explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel plant' reads as a new kind of plant; 'Novel' is a noun naming a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The name, from the biblical staff that blossomed, is both a Lawrence book title and a folk name for tall flowering spikes.

clue.text: Like a spy's role in a couple of tight spots?

blocks.note: first meaning: secret and underhand
second meaning, read literally: two awkward situations joined by 'and'

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: being 'in a hole' and 'in a corner' are both idioms for being in a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: Hole-and-corner describes furtive, clandestine dealings, the kind of covert work an espionage agent carries out.

clue.text: Put up with scoundrel, shamefaced

blocks.note: to put up a picture is to hang it
dog is an old word for a rogue, as in dirty dog

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates a rascal, looking embarrassed about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' reads as tolerate, but 'with' is only the join.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog look is guilty and ashamed, the sheepish expression of someone caught out.

clue.text: Magnificent old gold coin

blocks.note: first meaning: grand and impressive
second meaning: an English gold coin first minted under Edward III

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as praise for a coin; the adjective and the coin are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means imposing or stately, and was also the name of a medieval English gold piece worth a third of a pound.

clue.text: Rail against powerful businessman

blocks.note: a bar is a rail, as on a barrier
on can mean against, as in leaning on a wall

explanation.surface: Someone protests angrily about a business tycoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail against' reads as one verb, to complain bitterly, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron, as in press baron or oil baron, is a magnate who wields great influence in an industry.

clue.text: One married woman's no right to give cheek

indicators.note: having none of something means it is absent, so that letter is taken out of the name

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
standard abbreviation for married
a woman's first name
standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A married woman has no business being rude.
explanation.walkthrough: The woman is Prudence, who loses her R: I + M + P(R)UDENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheek in the sense of insolent talk is impudence, a bold lack of respect.

clue.text: Discover, after search, dog I'd raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the words lifts them so they read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a pug is a small breed of dog
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finds what their dog unearthed after a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig up information is to unearth it through investigation, discovering it after searching.

clue.text: Fair, steeplechaser's opening odds

indicators.note: the opening of a word is where it starts, so only its first letter is used

blocks.note: even means fair or balanced
first letter of steeplechaser

explanation.surface: A racing tipster rates a jumping horse's starting price as fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like the definition, but it is wordplay; the definition is at the other end. A steeplechaser is a horse racing over fences.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens is the betting price where the stake is matched one to one, the same odds either way.

clue.text: Making a mistake wearing the German pistol

indicators.note: someone wearing clothes has them around the body, so the outer word wraps the inner

blocks.note: der is a German word for the
erring means going wrong

explanation.surface: Someone blunders by wearing the German's pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: The German article goes around the error word: D-ERRING-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A derringer is a small pocket handgun, named after its American maker Henry Deringer.

clue.text: Shrub — gardener's first rambling rose

indicators.note: first means the leading letter of the word is taken
something rambling wanders without order, so the letters are scattered

blocks.note: first letter of gardener
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A gardener's top priority is a climbing rose bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling rose' is a real garden plant, which disguises 'rambling' as a description.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse is a spiny evergreen bush with yellow flowers, common on heaths.

clue.text: Information about a style of literature

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
re means concerning

explanation.surface: Details about a particular literary style.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category of artistic work, such as crime fiction or romance in books.

clue.text: Roman statesman is led up, struggling

indicators.note: something struggling is thrashing about, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A Roman politician is marched upward, resisting all the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepidus was a Roman politician, a member of the Second Triumvirate with Mark Antony and Octavian.
